slides.title: Introduction to the OCP Solution Provider Program
slides.subtitle: Bring open products, facilities and services to the people who need them.
slides.transcript: The Solution Provider Program helps people find and use OCP products, facilities, and services. Each offering has its own review and requirements. Understanding the differences makes the path easier to follow.

source_refs.basis: Single-module editorial revision; original teaching retained or consolidated.

slides.title: The OCP Solution Provider Program

source_refs.basis: Original video, figure, captions and transcript preserved unchanged on a media-only slide.

slides.transcript:
At OCP, our mission is to re-imagine data center, telco, and edge infrastructures

to achieve greater choice, customization and cost savings,

and OCP solution providers play a vital role in making that mission a reality

by delivering and supporting integrated solutions, providing

local engineering architecture resources for customers, establishing

and maintaining relationships with manufacturers of OCP products,

taking part in business planning sessions with the Foundation to better align

with your company's goals,

and of course, actively participating in the OCP Community.

Interested in becoming a solution provider?

The first thing you'll need to do is become an OCP Corporate Member

by signing the appropriate provider agreement and paying the appropriate fee.

The next step is to build

your product based on an approved OCP specification or design package

if you're a colo solution provider,

to complete the OCP Ready colo site assessment.

Once you do, you can enroll your product in the OCP product recognition program for

OCP Accepted approval, or submit your colo facility

site assessment to our incubation committee for OCP Ready recognition.

When your product, solution or facility has been approved, you can get started

marketing your OCP Accepted products, integrated solutions,

or OCP Ready facility on our marketplace and throughout the world.

By participating in the OCP Community as a solution provider,

you have the chance to bring greater efficiencies to your customers’

infrastructure, reach potential adopters, and most importantly,

contribute to reimagining our world's IT infrastructure.

Get started at opencompute.org.

slides.transcript: The Marketplace brings together approved Solution Providers and people looking for products or support. You can find hardware, chiplets, integrated solutions, professional services, facilities, and Experience Centers, including AI and edge offerings. A listing starts the conversation. Check the exact product, connections, support, and deployment needs with the provider.

slides.title: From product evidence to a listing
slides.transcript: OCP Accepted links a product to an approved specification or other contribution. Provide product information that shows that connection. The Foundation reviews it, with project expertise where needed. After approval, complete the required agreements and prepare the Marketplace listing. Recognition does not require disclosing design files; a design-package contribution is a separate route. It also does not approve every possible use of the product.

slides.title: Make the listing useful
slides.transcript: Give people a clear name, description, images, company logo, item-specific link, and contact. A video can help too. Keep the claims and information accurate as the offering changes. Quarterly listing analytics and business-development conversations can help you improve it. Analytics show activity; they do not identify every visitor or prove a sale.

slides.title: Know what a security review covers
slides.transcript: The Security Appraisal Framework and Enablement program, called Safe, uses a shared approach to firmware security review. A device manufacturer chooses an approved Security Review Provider. The reviewer supplies the required report, followed by program approval and listing. The Foundation issues the authorized marks. Check the device, firmware version, scope, and limits. This review is separate from product recognition and your own security checks.

slides.title: Facility recognition or firsthand experience
slides.transcript: OCP Ready recognition describes a facility through self-assessment, review, and approval. It leads to an authorized mark and Marketplace listing. An Experience Center lets people explore equipment or solutions firsthand. Its host proposes the scope to the Foundation. Both routes require Solution Provider participation, but they answer different needs.

slides.title: Choose the right OCP Ready path

cards.title: OCP Ready™ v1
cards.body: Facility readiness for OCP hardware and industry practices.

slides.transcript: OCP Ready version one covers facility readiness for OCP equipment. Version two for Hyperscale addresses larger colocation needs. You do not have to complete version one first. Discuss the facility and intended tenants with the Foundation before filling in the assessment. The operator supplies the evidence, the Data Center Facility team reviews it, and the Foundation approves it. This is not an OCP on-site audit.

slides.transcript: An Experience Center can be physical or virtual. The host provides the equipment and access, subject to its security and admission rules. The Foundation agrees the scope and services and approves the center. Project leaders may suggest opportunities. Adopters and channel partners can then explore how the solutions might work for them.

slides.title: Agree the terms before using a mark
slides.transcript: Tell the Foundation what you offer, who it serves, and what evidence you have. Confirm membership, the Solution Provider Agreement, and any recognition-specific agreements with someone authorized to sign. A certification mark is an approved program symbol with rules for its use. Use only the marks and claims your agreements allow.

items: Match the program to the product, facility or service.
Show clear evidence and complete the required agreements.

slides.transcript: Products, facilities, security reviews, and Experience Centers each have a different purpose. Choose the right route, provide clear evidence, and agree the terms with the Foundation. A useful listing makes that work understandable to the people who may use it.

lms_catalog.title: Introduction to the OCP Solution Provider Program
lms_catalog.short_description: Find the right OCP program for products, facilities and services, and understand the path to a Marketplace listing.
lms_catalog.overview: The OCP Solution Provider Program connects products, facilities and services with people who can use them. Understand what each recognition means, what evidence supports it, and how participation leads to a clear, useful Marketplace listing.
lms_catalog.duration_note: Includes narration, videos, reading and the final two-question check. Optional close inspection of screenshots and exploration of linked resources may take longer.

modules.summary: Explore Marketplace products, chiplets, integrated solutions, services, facilities and Experience Centers. Distinguish OCP Accepted product recognition, S.A.F.E. firmware security review and OCP Ready facility recognition. Follow the evidence, review and agreement steps, learn what Experience Centers offer, and understand membership, fees, authorized marks and keeping listing information current.
